T4.2.message: liṅga has many senses in mw-linga.md: 'mark, sign', Śiva's emblem or icon, '(in Sāṃkhya) = prakṛti', and 'anything having an origin and therefore liable to be destroyed again'. The data picks 'a mark, sign...' as the sense, but the meaning just says 'liṅga' and the c3 note gives 'mark, sign; the liṅga'. Without a gloss, a reader will most likely think of the stone Śiva-liṅga, and that is probably not what 'this world which has the liṅga as its nature' means here. linga-purana-1-3.md (1.3.1-4) treats liṅga as the manifest, marked world (prakṛti) that comes from the unmarked Śiva. That sense, and the MW sense 'having an origin and liable to be destroyed', fit this line. Gita Press leaves it untranslated too, so this is not clearly wrong. A human should decide whether the contextual sense needs spelling out.
T4.2.suggested_fix: In words.w14 (meaning or notes) and c3.note, say which sense of liṅga is meant, e.g. 'liṅga here is the visible, marked form, the world that arises and dissolves, a sign of the unseen Śiva'.
